article.headline: A Swedish Studio's Site Proves WebGPU Has Arrived
article.lede: The website for Shader Development Studio looks like something recovered from a 1987 corporate training film — blocky period typography, confident geometric shapes, measured pacing. The aesthetic is entirely deliberate, and it runs on a rendering engine that barely existed five years ago.
article.body:
The site, shader.se, is built on Three.js running its **WebGPU** back-end rather than the older *WebGL* path that has underpinned browser-based 3D since 2011. *WebGPU* is the W3C's next-generation GPU API for browsers, which reached critical support across all major browsers in 2025; it offers lower CPU overhead, direct compute access, and a more modern architecture than its predecessor. In production deployments it has remained rare — shader.se is one of the more widely cited examples of it powering a real, client-facing website rather than a hobbyist experiment.

The site's signature achievement is its scene transitions. These are not CSS fades or JavaScript dissolves but coordinated GPU passes in which lighting, geometry, and post-processing effects shift together without seams. The effect depends on *Three Shading Language (TSL)*, Three.js's *node-graph* shader abstraction, which compiles down to *WGSL* (WebGPU's own shading language) at runtime. The 1987 aesthetic makes the contrast visceral: anachronistic visuals rendered by machinery that would have been inconceivable in 1987.

**Shader Sweden AB**, trading as Shader Development Studio, was founded in 2021 by Filip Kantedal and Simon Hedlund, two Media Technology graduates from Linköping University in Norrköping, a Swedish city of roughly 140,000. The studio operates with two principals and a network of collaborators assembled per project; client work ranges from 3D product-planning tools to interactive visualizations for Swedish public institutions.

The site won Awwwards Site of the Day in April 2026, scoring 9.40 out of 10 for animations and transitions — the category that jury members most consistently marked exceptional. Coverage from the WebGPU developer community framed it as a practical argument for the TSL workflow: composing shader logic as node graphs rather than hand-written *WGSL*, in the same way design tools abstract Bézier curves from the underlying math. Jim Raptis (@d__raptis), a Greek design engineer and serial product founder who curates technically impressive web interactions for roughly 30,000 developers, was characteristically terse in his verdict.

concepts.definition: The W3C's next-generation GPU API for web browsers, reaching broad support across major browsers in 2025. It offers lower CPU overhead, direct access to GPU compute, and a more modern programming model than the older WebGL standard it is gradually supplanting.

A browser-native API for GPU-accelerated 2D and 3D graphics, standardized around 2011 and based on OpenGL ES. It has been the backbone of browser 3D for over a decade but carries architectural constraints that WebGPU is designed to overcome.

A node-based shader abstraction built into Three.js. Rather than writing raw shader code by hand, developers connect logical nodes in a graph; TSL compiles the result to either WGSL (for WebGPU) or GLSL (for WebGL) at runtime, making shaders more composable and portable across rendering back-ends.

WebGPU Shading Language — the shader programming language native to WebGPU, analogous to GLSL in the WebGL world. Shaders written in WGSL describe how individual vertices and pixels should be processed on the GPU.

A visual programming pattern in which logic is expressed as a directed graph of connected nodes rather than lines of text code. Widely used in shader editors, VFX tools, and game engines; Three Shading Language applies the same idea to browser-based GPU materials.

A daily award given by Awwwards, a competition and gallery that recognizes exceptional web design and development. The designation is a widely watched signal of technical and creative quality among designers and front-end developers; jury scores span design, usability, creativity, and content.

repos.summary: Three.js is the most widely used JavaScript library for 3D graphics in the browser, abstracting over WebGL and (now) WebGPU with a scene graph, material system, loaders, and post-processing. The WebGPU back-end and TSL were introduced as its next-generation rendering path. Shader.se's entire visual layer is built on top of it.
